questions.question: Which of the following is classified as a behavioural adaptation in animals?
options: Having a thick layer of blubber under the skin
Being nocturnal and active only at night
Possessing sharp claws for catching prey
Having striped fur for camouflage

questions.question: Why is maintaining high biodiversity crucial for an ecosystem?
options: It ensures that only the strongest species can survive
It is important for keeping habitats healthy and stable
It decreases the overall number of food chains
It prevents any natural changes from occurring in the environment

questions.question: What is meant by the term 'gene pool' in biology?
options: The physical location where frogs and insects breed
The total number of individual organisms in a habitat
The range of DNA present within a species
The collection of physical adaptations in an ecosystem

questions.question: Why do ecologists use sampling to estimate populations in an area rather than counting every single organism?
options: Because sampling is the only way to find out what species eat
Because counting every individual organism would be impossible
Because sampling automatically prevents any animals from migrating
Because animals cannot be seen without specialized sampling traps

questions.question: What are quadrats, and what are they primarily used to sample?
options: Square frames used to sample plants or slow-moving animals
Long nets used to capture fast-flying birds
Deep traps used to collect nocturnal burrowing mammals
Sensors used to measure the moisture level of soil

questions.question: Why is most sampling using quadrats carried out randomly?
options: To make sure the sampling takes as much time as possible
To avoid bias in the results
To ensure that only the rarest plants are counted
To guarantee that every quadrat contains the same number of organisms

questions.question: What is the main purpose of using a classification key in ecological studies?
options: To measure the biomass of a population
To count the number of decomposers in the soil
To identify different species of organisms
To randomly place quadrats in a field

questions.question: What makes up an ecosystem?
options: Only the non-living surroundings in a specific habitat
A community of organisms interacting with each other and their non-living surroundings
A single species of animal and the food it eats
The weather conditions and temperature of an area over a year

questions.question: Organisms in an ecosystem are described as interdependent. What does this mean?
options: They do not require any resources from their environment to survive
They rely on different habitats during different times of the year
They depend upon each other for the things they need to survive
They compete so fiercely that only one species can survive

questions.question: Why are decomposers essential for the survival of other living organisms in an ecosystem?
options: They make food directly from sunlight for the herbivores
They break down dead organisms and recycle useful substances for reuse
They control the population of large predators
They provide shade for young plants to grow

questions.question: What is the definition of biodiversity?
options: The study of how animals behave in the wild
The total mass of all plants in a specific ecosystem
A measure of the range of living organisms
The speed at which energy flows through a food chain

questions.question: Which of the following is a physical adaptation of a plant?
options: Growing towards a source of light
Releasing seeds only during autumn
Opening flowers only during the daytime
Having spines to deter consumers

questions.question: Which of the following is a behavioural adaptation in plants?
options: Having shallow or deep roots to absorb water
Growing towards light
Developing thick waxy leaves to reduce water loss
Producing toxic chemicals in their stems

questions.question: What is biomass?
options: The total volume of water stored inside a plant's roots
The mass of living material in one or more organisms
The number of organisms at the top of a food chain
The energy lost as heat to the surroundings

questions.question: What do pyramids of biomass show?
options: The number of individual organisms at each stage in a food chain
The speed at which food is digested by consumers
The biomass of organisms at each stage in a food chain
The physical height of plants in a habitat

questions.question: What do the scaled bars in a pyramid of numbers represent?
options: The total dry mass of all organisms in the habitat
The number of organisms at each trophic level
The amount of energy transferred between levels
The physical size of the individual organisms
